newsitem.title: UK: Syria, Algeria set December oil selling prices.
newsitem.headline: Syria, Algeria set December oil selling prices.

text.p: Algeria has finalised agreement with term lifters for December oil prices which were set at Dated Brent +72/+75 cents for Saharan Blend crude, traders said.
This was down from November's Dated Brent +80 cents for the gasoline-rich Algerian crude.
Syria's state owned Sytrol also reached agreement to sell its Syrian light crude at Dated Brent -5 cents, unchanged from November, they added.
One trader said lifters were happy with the outcome, which took into account higher differentials for sour Mediterranean benchmark Urals currently valued at a 57/58 discount to Dated Brent.

The traders said negotiations still continued with term lifters on Syrian heavy crude Soueidie with no definite number agreed although Sytrol had indicated readiness to lower its price from November's Dated -$3.90 a barrel.
One trader said the end of the summer bitumen-producing season meant demand for Soueidie was low at this time of year.

A European lifter of Libyan crude said he expected NOC to roll over November prices into December for its light crudes and possibly cut the price of heavier grades when it sets official prices sometime next week.
